Then he actually said that.

In the latest episode of Jennifer Welch's "I've Had It" podcast, Handler launched a sweeping and sharp critique of the Trump administration, and during the conversation about White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, Welch reminded listeners, "We on this podcast have decided that he is worse than Ted Cruz to have to [have sex with]."

Handler seized on the topic and turned it into a game, asking Welch to choose among the late Senator Lindsey Graham (Republican, South Carolina), Senator Ted Cruz (Republican, Texas), and Miller, the key architect of Trump's anti-immigration policies.

Welch asked, "The least wanting to [have sex with]?" then said, "You have to pick Stephen Miller."

Handler then escalated, asking Welch to pick a sexual partner from Miller, the world's richest man Elon Musk, and Nazi Germany dictator Hitler (if he were still alive).

Welch said, "Damn, that's really a dirty trick."

Welch ultimately picked Musk, and Handler immediately replied, "Yeah, I think that is the correct choice."

After chatting for a while, the conversation eventually returned to the topic of "MAGA men," with Welch saying these people had become "completely useless" because of their double standards and inability to protect their own wives.

Welch recalled how Trump had insulted Cruz's wife Heidi during the 2016 Republican primary, yet Cruz later went all out to support his former adversary.

Welch said, "I mean, it's really completely unprincipled and spineless."

Handler agreed: "They have absolutely no agency. Back then I thought a lot more about Ted Cruz's wife than those two losers' wives, because how is it possible— you guys have kids together. You actually let your kids' father go hug tightly the person who once spoke to you like that. Honestly, this really is like marrying a snake, and he has no direction at all, Ted Cruz is really disgusting. He doesn't even count as a snake, because at least a snake knows how to bite."

Welch then brought up the game again, asking Handler to pick between Cruz and Miller as the one "more willing to [have sex with]."

Handler answered, "Stephen, I think I could handle him. You know what I mean? Like I feel like I could take him, I'm quite fit and he looks very weak, otherwise he wouldn't behave like that."

Handler added, "So, Ted Cruz, to me, whether his physique or everything else, is repulsive and disgusting. Stephen Miller is the same, but he's like a little kid, something really bad must have happened to him, some really terrible thing, to make him turn out like this. And I have a chance to physically subdue him, maybe even take his life."

Welch asked, "And sexually abuse him?"

Handler said, "In a sexual context, yes, in a sexual context, I would."
